title: Linux’s 35th Anniversary and the Open Frontier
content:
Dear OSI community,

I’d be remiss if I didn’t open by wishing Linux a happy 35th birthday. I can’t pretend to have accomplished nearly as much by the age of 35 as Linux has, but neither was I nurtured by such a vast community of contributors and supporters. We can’t lose sight of that. Open Source is what it is because of the people who led us here, and keep us here. We all joined the community for different reasons, but many of us stayed because of the relationships and partnerships we built along the way, connections that run deeper than the code.

I get asked almost every day about the future of Open Source. One of my consistent answers is that people who love writing code will keep wanting to write code together. I believe that’s as true today as it was before AI tools, Git, the OSI, the World Wide Web, Perl, or C entered the chat. But we’re also passing through a moment of unquestionable transition. AI tools and agents are testing our processes, policies, laws, licenses, and beliefs in real time.
creator: Nick Vidal

title: Open Weights Are Good. Open Source Is Better.
content:
By this point, you’ve seen the news about open-weight AI models and the debate over their security, efficiency, and impact on both local and national economies. Scores of businesses have come out in support of open-weights, highlighting how they increase access to advanced AI and maintain competition in the market. This is all true, and shedding light on these arguments benefits the Open Source community. 

At the same time, we must take this moment, when openness in AI is making headlines, to educate policymakers, producers, and users of these technologies about what open-weight and Open Source AI mean for the four software freedoms: the freedom to use, study, modify, and share without the need to ask for permission from the rights holder. Those are the core tenets of the Open Source movement that power the technology we use every day. Those are the tenets that built the Open Source ecosystem with a demand-side value of $8.8 trillion. It’s those tenets that we should strive to uphold in this next phase of technological development.

title: We Must Open the Frontier: OSI, OFAI Support Calls for the U.S. to Develop More Open Models
content:
The Open Source Initiative joins the Open Forum for AI (OFAI) in supporting calls for the U.S. to develop more open models because they promote competition in AI through local control and lower costs. The OFAI is a university-led, collaborative initiative that aims to bend the arc toward human-centered, responsible, transparent, and ethical AI. Led by Carnegie Mellon University, the OFAI includes university representatives from across the country as well as nonprofit voices and individual fellows from industry and government. As the policy lead, we collaborated with other OFAI members to lay out the benefits of Open Source AI and open-weight models in comparison to closed, proprietary ones. 

The statement asserts that the U.S. needs more “focus, investment, and collaboration from the full breadth of the innovation pipeline to accelerate the development of open models. This will require a strategic approach that moves beyond the status quo, bringing together new partners, both technical and non-technical, from across industry, academia, and government.”

Link to statement:  https://www.openforumai.org/news/us-needs-more-open-models

title: OSI brings the State of the Source to All Things Open 2026
content:
The Open Source Initiative (OSI) is coming to All Things Open with a track designed to connect developers with the big policy conversations shaping our ecosystem. This year’s State of the Source looks at Open Source from several perspectives. Hear about OSI’s priorities for 2027, get a practical introduction to Open Source licensing and compliance, and discuss Open Source sustainability. We’ll also explore the latest public policy developments affecting Open Source, examine the state of Open Source AI, and discuss how OSI can strengthen Open Source education and advocacy.

All Things Open is one of the largest Open Source technology conferences in the United States, bringing together a technical and engaged audience of developers, engineers, community leaders, students, educators, executives, and other Open Source practitioners.

All Things Open 2026 takes place October 19–20 in Raleigh, North Carolina, part of the Research Triangle, one of the country’s leading centers for technology and Open Source innovation.
